title: harbor-financial-integration-call-notes-2026-03-22
content:
Call notes: Harbor Financial integration kickoff — 2026-03-22
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Harbor), Priya Shah (Harbor), Marisol Chen (Redwood CS), Derek Patel (SE), Samir Rao (Eng)

Topline: Harbor wants to run customer-facing chat + document search via embeddings. Primary constraints: strict data residency (EU), SOC2 + PCI scope, and hard latency target for chat <250ms p50 for short prompts. They are evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) vs Dedicated; initial preference toward Private due to their compliance posture.

Customer background/context:
- Mid-sized online bank, EU customers only, heavy compliance.
- Existing infra: Azure with private peering to select partners. Wants L2 isolation and KMS integration.
- Current use case: customer support assistant + knowledge base search (documents + transcripts). Expected 200-500 qps at peak after rollout (estimated).

Requirements/asks from Harbor:
- Data residency: all inference and logs must remain in eu-west-1 region.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS/HSM).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for production endpoints; latency SLO for chat p50 <250ms, p95 <700ms for typical 256-token contexts.
- Security: audit logs for queries, redact PII in logs, ability to disable logging for selected routes.
- Model: initially use open Llama-2-70b quantized variant (or similar) with embeddings model for search.
- Cost target: <$0.02/query average (post-optimizations) - they're cost sensitive.

Technical notes / gotchas we surfaced:
- Quantized 70B model on Private: we need to validate latency on target GPUs (A10/A100) and CPU fallback paths. Continuous KV cache + prefix caching likely needed for chat to hit p50 250ms.
- Batching trade-offs: to meet p50 <250ms we'll need small batching windows; that increases unit cost. Consider per-route policy: low-latency routes with higher cost vs batched cheaper route for async flows.
- KMS: Private supports customer KMS but need SRE confirm HSM requirements for Harbor's audits.
- Audit log redaction: can support via Transparent Data Processing (TDP) hook, but requires integration with their PII tagging. Need to confirm if Harbor will ship PII rules or want Redwood to provide default heuristics.
- Embeddings size & recall: for doc search we recommended 1536-d dense embeddings (open model). Need to benchmark similarity recall and sharding strategy for 500k docs. They plan nightly reindex + nearline updates.
- Fall-back model variants: propose two-tier model routing: smaller/cheaper 13B or 33B for non-critical routes; 70B quantized for critical customer-facing chat. Need to document version pinning & rollout plan.

Open questions to resolve:
1) Exact GPU instance types available in their Azure region and whether customer will accept shared tenancy for Dedicated vs fully isolated for Private. (Action: Derek to confirm with infra partner)
2) KMS/HSM compliance level - do they need FIPS 140-2/3 HSM-backed keys or will Azure Key Vault suffice? (Action: Marisol to ask Alex by 2026-03-24)
3) Target qps ramp timeline - they gave broad 3-6 month plan; need concrete monthly ramp to size capacity. (Action: Alex to share ramp plan before next sync)
4) Data retention policy for logs/embeddings: Harbor asked for 30-day default but may need longer for audits. (Action: Priya to confirm required retention windows)

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Run latency benchmark matrix for 70B quantized on candidate instance types (A10, A100 40GB, A100 80GB). Include p50/p95 and cost-per-token. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-03-30.
- Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and provide reference architecture for Private deployment with customer-managed keys. Owner: Marisol. Due: 2026-03-24.
- Draft routing policy proposal: low-latency path (minimal batching, dedicated pool) vs cost-optimized path (batched, cached). Include rollout canary steps and failover rules. Owner: Derek. Due: 2026-03-29.
- Prepare a short one-pager for Harbor explaining options (Private vs Dedicated) with trade-offs (latency, cost, compliance) and recommended initial config. Owner: Marisol + Derek. Due: 2026-03-26.
- Share evaluation harness & sample benchmark script for their infra team to run locally if they want independent numbers. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-03-25.

Risks & notes:
- If Harbor insists on p50 250ms for 70B across all traffic, cost will be high unless we can exploit caching aggressively. Need to set expectation re: cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Embeddings recall risk: if docs have heavy domain-specific tokens, open embedding quality may be lower; propose adding a small re-ranking model pipeline and a few manual eval prompts.
- Migration concerns: Harbor has legacy search infra built on Elastic; we should propose phased rollout (search as augmentation) before chat goes live.

Follow-up meeting: propose 1-week cadence. Next sync tentative 2026-03-29 to review benchmarks and KMS answer.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Prep sample config: private-deploy config snippet with kms_key_id placeholder, region eu-west-1, model_pin: llama-2-70b-q4_0.
- Check RDW internal playbook for PII redaction integration (doc id CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Pull recent Dedicated pricing sheet for EU and include estimated monthly for 500 qps baseline.

End of notes.
